To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a hybrid system can reduce fuel consumption and pollution with respect to a system based on diesel generators only.

the optimal energy mix for a hybrid photovoltaic-wild-diesel system is not necessarily the one with the maximum possible contribution of the renewable sources, but that it is a function of the system constraints and of the actual component characteristics, and that the presence of batteries in a hybrid system could lead to further reductions of the fuel consumption.

the optimization of a hybrid energy system for an off-grid application is not necessarily that including the maximum amount of renewable energy sources; the optimal solution is that providing a suitable energy mix among the different sources and the batteries; the batteries are able to reduce the fuel consumption and to decrease the engine transitory use.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a more realistic approach to the design of hybrid energy systems, which can lead to the identification of optimal energy mixes and to the definition of the most suitable sizing strategy for each application.
the development and testing of an optimization strategy for the sizing of hybrid PV-winddiesel stand-alone systems, which can be used to provide the best solution for a specific application.
a new approach to the sizing of a hybrid PV-diesel-wind system, which takes into account the actual characteristics of the components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimization of a hybrid system is a complex task and the optimal configuration depends on a number of parameters, including actual machine data and system constraints.
a hybrid system, properly designed according to the present approach, is a promising solution to reduce supply costs and environmental impact in the electrification of off-grid users.
, for this case study, a hybrid system with a 50% contribution from renewable energy sources and 100 kWh battery storage was the optimal configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimization of a hybrid system should not be based on the maximization of the contribution of renewable sources, but should rather be performed by means of a cost analysis, which would allow the identification of the optimal energy mix between the different energy sources.

the present analysis could be considered a step towards more accurate sizing approaches of hybrid systems, which could be used in the design phase of a new stand-alone system or for the upgrade of an existing one.
, in a remote, off-grid application, the optimal energy mix for a hybrid system is not necessarily that including the maximum possible contribution from renewable sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal configuration of a hybrid system depends on the actual component characteristics and on realistic system constraints.
a hybrid system can be economically advantageous for a user, but only if it is properly designed.
the optimal energy mix between diesel, PV, wind, and batteries is strongly dependent on the actual component characteristics and on realistic cost functions.
